anchors.paper_title: Modeling short visual events through the BOLD moments video fMRI dataset and metadata
anchors.reason: The paper describes the BOLD Moments fMRI companion dataset (BMD) using the same videos, not the EEG data in EMD, so it is related work rather than this dataset's data paper.

metadata.methods_description: Raw EEG and simultaneous eye-tracking data were recorded over multiple sessions while subjects maintained central fixation during presentation of 3-second videos with audio. Subjects saw the training videos 6 times and the test videos 24 times. Data are provided in BIDS format, along with preprocessed EEG and eye-tracking derivatives and stimulus metadata.

citation_details.title: A large dataset of human EEG responses to short naturalistic videos for studying dynamic visual event processing
citation_details.author: Alessandro T. Gifford, Pablo Oyarzo, Anne W. Zonneveld, Christina Sartzetaki, Iris I. A. Groen, Radoslaw Martin Cichy
citation_details.abstract: Vision neuroscience has experienced a surge in the collection and use of large-scale datasets of brain responses to naturalistic images. However, static images lack the temporal dimension essential for understanding how vision is solved in the brain during dynamic real life settings. To facilitate the study of the neural correlates of dynamic visual event perception, we introduce the EEG Moments Dataset (EMD). EMD consists of 128-channel EEG responses and eye-tracking recordings of 6 human participants viewing 1,102 short naturalistic videos (3-second long; with audio track) while maintaining central fixation. We show that EMD's EEG responses well encode stimulus-related information, exhibit a temporal correspondence with the video stimuli, and have a rich representational content revealed by brain encoding models based on different feature spaces. Furthermore, complemented by the BOLD Moments Dataset (BMD) - an existing large-scale dataset of human functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) responses for the same videos - EMD enables spatio-temporally resolved investigations of brain responses to dynamic visual events. We release EMD's EEG and eye-tracking data in both raw and preprocessed format, along with the 1,102 video stimuli, and rich stimulus metadata. Finally, we provide an interactive code tutorial to familiarize with EMD's preprocessed data, stimuli, and stimulus metadata.
